executive_summary.headline: OpenAI says its models refuted a decades-old computer science assumption, and video creators are making it easy to follow.
executive_summary.body: Two Minute Papers walks through OpenAI's exponential time hypothesis paper, and TheAIGRID explains all three announced discoveries (math, computer science, physics) in plain English. OpenAI says outside researchers act as shepherds for the results, and it opened a Rosalind Academic Plan for labs the same week.

executive_summary.headline: Frontier capability got faster and cheaper at once: Gemini 4 Carbon took #1 on a leaderboard and GPT-6.1 Terra undercut Opus on build time.
executive_summary.body: Google says Carbon is #1 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, and Berman covers the launch. Nick Saraev's side-by-side found Terra averaged 23:43 per build against 43:52 for Opus 5.5, at OpenAI's listed $1 and $5 per million tokens.

executive_summary.headline: Builders are shipping real businesses and creative pipelines: a $60M ARR voice front office for trades, Claude-built 3D worlds, and AI relighting for film.
executive_summary.body: YC's Broccoli talk covers 500+ customers and a $30M Series B for an AI front office that books home-service jobs. Skill Leap AI has Claude build three 3D worlds in Blender and Unreal, and Curious Refuge shows how to relight a finished shot with AI.

top_picks.title: OpenAI Claims It Just Did The Impossible
top_picks.summary: Two Minute Papers walks through OpenAI's paper arguing that the exponential time hypothesis, a decades-old assumption behind hundreds of results in computer science, is false. The host says expert review is still underway and that the proof looks increasingly convincing. The same OpenAI announcement includes new results in harmonic analysis and quantum field theory.
top_picks.author: Two Minute Papers

secondary_urls.label: OpenAI paper (ETH is false, Oct 25 2026 preprint)
OpenAI: three new discoveries in mathematics, computer science and physics
OpenAI: Rosalind Academic Plan for academic labs
TheAIGRID plain-English walkthrough of the three discoveries

key_takeaways: OpenAI announced three discoveries at once: a proof of the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension (which also resolves Kakeya and Stein restriction), a refutation of the exponential time hypothesis, and a result in quantum field theory.
The host explains the 3-satisfiability problem with a cat, a dog and a dancing robot, then says many papers assume the hypothesis, so a proof would ripple through complexity theory.
OpenAI says outside researchers act as 'shepherds' for the computer science and physics results, and it released the math output for specialists to work through.
suggested_actions: Send the seven-minute video to your scientists as an easy opener for a conversation about AI as a research collaborator.
Ask each research group for one open problem in simulation, materials or building physics and try a frontier model on it this month.
Look at OpenAI's Rosalind Academic Plan page for how labs get sponsored access to a science-tuned model.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: When a model settles a question that stood for decades, skeptical scientists start asking what it could do for their own backlog. Run a one-week 'stubborn problem' sprint where each researcher brings the question they have parked longest and tries it against the best model available.

top_picks.title: Building AI for the $650B Home Services Market
top_picks.summary: Broccoli's founders tell how an AI front office for home-services businesses grew from zero to an expected $60 million ARR in two years. The AI answers calls, follows up on leads and books appointments across voice, text and SMS for more than 500 customers. YC says the booked-job run rate for its customers is over $1 billion a year, after the founders visited 140 contractors to find the real problem.
top_picks.author: YC Root Access
key_takeaways: Broccoli serves 500+ customers and expects to end the year above $60 million ARR, up from zero two years ago, after a $30 million Series B.
The company reached this after an earlier EV startup missed product-market fit and the founders went door to door with 140 contractors.
The pitch is a complete front office: every call answered, every lead followed up, every appointment scheduled.
suggested_actions: Watch the 'Discovering the Real Problem' chapter (14:49) and list the missed-call moments in your own customer queues.
Prototype a voice and SMS follow-up flow for one inbound line using an off-the-shelf voice model.
Ask your field sales or service team which calls go unanswered after hours.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: The winning move was picking one unglamorous job, answering the phone and booking the work, and doing it perfectly. Any dispatch, quoting or service-request line is a candidate: give it a voice agent that books straight into the calendar and measure booked jobs, not call minutes.

top_picks.title: Google "Carbon" just won everything...
top_picks.summary: Google says Gemini 4 Carbon ranks #1 on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and leads on cybersecurity and long-horizon tasks. Berman walks through the launch benchmarks in 14 minutes. It arrives about two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon's release, starts rolling out to cyber defenders, and Google says wider access for developers, businesses and consumers is coming.
top_picks.author: Matthew Berman
key_takeaways: Google's own post claims the #1 spot on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 and state-of-the-art long-horizon capability.
Reuters and CNET count about two weeks since Argon's release, while TheAIGRID counts four weeks since Argon's announcement; either way it is a fast cadence.
Access starts with Google's Fairwind program for defenders, with broader availability announced as coming soon.
suggested_actions: Add Carbon to your model bake-off list now so a long-horizon task is ready the day access opens.
Pick one multi-hour workflow (a refactor, a data migration, a literature sweep) as the test case.
Compare Carbon's long-horizon results with GPT-6.1 Terra on the same task.

top_picks.title: OpenAI Made Vibe Coding Too Cheap It Feels Unfair
top_picks.summary: Nick Saraev ran GPT-6.1 Terra in Codex and Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the same prompts and found Terra finished builds in 23:43 on average against 43:52 for Opus. He tests a game, a landing page, a Minecraft-style build, computer use and vision, then gives a verdict on when to use each. OpenAI lists Terra at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.
top_picks.author: Nick Saraev

secondary_urls.label: OpenAI Help Center: GPT-6.1 Terra release notes and pricing

key_takeaways: Average build time was 23 minutes 43 seconds for Terra and 43 minutes 52 seconds for Opus 5.5, with each model in its own coding harness at max effort.
Chapters cover Stormwatch, The Long Night, a Minecraft build, Neon Drift and a landing page, then computer use, vision and factual error rate.
The video ends with a verdict on when to reach for Terra and when for Opus.
suggested_actions: Copy his setup: one prompt, two harnesses, a side-by-side landing page of results.
Run your own weekly internal build on both models and track time and cost per task.
Try Terra for screen-driven chores such as form filling and report pulls, since it is built for computer use.

top_picks.title: Claude Can Now Create 3D
top_picks.summary: Skill Leap AI has Claude build three 3D worlds using Blender and Unreal Engine on a laptop with a Claude subscription, and shows each from first prompt to finished scene. The pitch is that people who have never touched either tool can now stage game worlds and 3D scenes by describing them.
top_picks.author: Skill Leap AI
key_takeaways: Three complete 3D worlds are built with Blender and Unreal Engine, with the prompts shown from first request to final scene.
Everything runs on a laptop with a Claude subscription, no separate 3D service.
The creator pairs the video with 21 ready-made builds to copy.
suggested_actions: Install Blender (free) and ask Claude Code to build a small scene of a product or facility you know well.
Try a walkthrough scene of a building envelope or a product install as a visual for your next internal demo.
Reuse the prompts shown in the video as a template for your own scenes.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: A 3D scene used to need a specialist and a week. Describe a product in a room, a facility layout or a customer's building and get a walkable draft by the end of a meeting, then hand the best one to a designer.

top_picks.title: The NEW Lighting Workflow Changing Filmmaking (Full AI Tutorial)
top_picks.summary: Curious Refuge shows an AI workflow that relights a finished shot, so a crew can shoot with rough lighting and set the final look in post. The 11-minute tutorial covers live-action scenes and gray-box scenes, with a written breakdown on the Curious Refuge blog. It also mentions Idris Elba's company Akuna partnering with Google and Curious Refuge to train 1,000 aspiring filmmakers in Africa.
top_picks.author: Curious Refuge

secondary_urls.label: Curious Refuge: how to relight videos using AI

key_takeaways: Rough on-set lighting is enough; the look is set in post-production with the AI workflow.
The method works on live-action footage and on gray-box scenes inside an AI production pipeline.
Curious Refuge, Akuna and Google are training 1,000 aspiring filmmakers in Africa on these workflows.
suggested_actions: Run the workflow on one product video and change its lighting three ways.
Use the blog breakdown as a checklist for your marketing or training video team.
Shoot the next training clip with whatever light is in the room and relight afterward.

sections.title: Tool and Model Demos
sections.description: New models and tools shown working on video this week, with a bias to things you can run yourself.

items.title: Deepseek crushed everyone
items.summary: Berman calls DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 the best open-source model available and opens with a build test: an interactive 3D mechanical watch where hovering shows each part's name and function and the pieces fit and move. DeepSeek describes the update as stronger, faster and shorter-winded than the previous Flash, with API pricing unchanged. The video is sponsored by CoreWeave.
items.author: Matthew Berman

items.title: Deepseek 4.1 Flash on 2 DGX Sparks changed my life
items.summary: Alex Finn links two DGX Sparks in his home lab and runs DeepSeek 4.1 Flash on them to see whether a pair of desktop boxes can replace cloud subscriptions for a full coding workflow. He says he is blown away by the result. Chapters cover unboxing, clustering, loading the model and testing the final build, and Micro Center sponsors the video.
items.author: Alex Finn

items.title: Grok Bot just released a MASSIVE update
items.summary: Grok Bot now lets users build custom pages and dashboards, which Alex Finn says fixes the main problem of running many bots at once: knowing which bot owns what. He shows his own dashboard and ends with a copy-and-paste prompt that sets up the same organization in Grok Bot.
items.author: Alex Finn

items.title: ChatGPT Just Changed A LOT AGAIN (Here's What's New)
items.summary: Riley Brown's weekly agent roundup leads with texting your ChatGPT Dot from iMessage, which gives you control of Codex from your phone's messages. It also covers ChatGPT plan and usage-limit changes, the Siri AI beta, Gemini 4 Carbon, Grok Bot updates and wider access to Claude Duet.
items.author: Riley Brown

items.title: 3,000 Tokens/Sec Locally: Testing the ZGX Fury
items.summary: Sam Witteveen tests HP's ZGX Fury, a deskside machine with 748 GB of memory and an NVIDIA GB300 chip that he describes as a mini data center a whole team can share. The title reports 3,000 tokens per second locally. HP sponsored the video and supplied a loaner unit.
items.author: Sam Witteveen

items.title: AI News: The Only 6 Stories Worth Knowing This Week
items.summary: Matt Wolfe's weekly roundup covers GPT-6.1 Terra's faster, cheaper computer use, Gemini 4 Carbon, Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights, a hands-on test of Google's Genie 4 world model, and OpenAI's mathematics breakthrough. It also opens with Anthropic's IPO filing. Links to the launch posts are in the description.
items.author: Matt Wolfe

secondary_urls.label: OpenAI: three new discoveries in mathematics, computer science and physics

sections.title: Tutorials Worth Copying
sections.description: Step-by-step builds and stacks you can follow this week.

items.title: My AI Setup Feels Like Cheating (Here's All of It)
items.summary: Riley Brown shares the agent stack he settled on after spending $10,000 testing tools, and when he reaches for Claude Code, Codex or Grok Bot. The 31-minute video covers Claude Projects, app building, slides, video editing with Claude and voice with Dots, with Composio sharing skills and plugins across the platforms. Superhuman sponsors the video.
items.author: Riley Brown
key_takeaways: He splits work between Claude Code, Codex and Grok Bot by task type, starting with Claude Projects.
Composio sits in the middle so skills and plugins carry between agent platforms.
Use cases include building apps, designing slides, editing video and running administrative tasks.
suggested_actions: List your top five repeat tasks and assign each to a single agent, as he does.
Set up one shared skills layer so a workflow built once runs in any agent.
Grab his resource list and copy the first project setup.

items.title: The Biggest Faceless Content Opportunity: AI Vtuber Avatars
items.summary: Nick Saraev shows a fully AI-generated vtuber-style video, built by creating pixel-art character assets and recombining them rather than using a video model. He explains why stylized characters such as anime work better than realistic faces and why he used a Japanese voice through Fish Audio.
items.author: Nick Saraev
key_takeaways: Assets are generated first and recombined into an animated character, with no video model in the loop.
Stylized looks (anime, watercolor, cartoon) read better than realistic faces and avoid the uncanny valley.
Voice comes from Fish Audio, and he chose Japanese on purpose for the format.
suggested_actions: Make a 30-second avatar explainer for one product feature.
Pick one art style and keep it across every asset for a consistent series.
Try the same pipeline for a training clip with a recurring mascot.

sections.title: Use Cases to Borrow
sections.description: Agents, automation and creative pipelines running in real creator, small-business and personal workflows.

items.title: my bots just BROKE Wall St...
items.summary: Wes Roth builds an AI research desk in Grok Bot with a chief of staff, specialist analysts, group chats, scheduled routines and skills learned by watching him work. He runs it as a simulated paper-trading hedge fund, and the video is sponsored by SpaceX. The 27-minute guide takes viewers from a first bot to a connected AI workforce.
items.author: Wes Roth
items.enterprise_translation: A named desk of agents with a chief of staff is a small research department that works overnight. Give a team of analyst bots a standing brief, such as competitor watch or supplier news, and read the morning digest instead of running the search yourself.

items.title: I Rebuilt This AI Agency Coaching Business (in 1 Week)
items.summary: Liam Ottley flies to Javea, Spain, to rebuild a friend's agency-coaching business with AI in one week. The founder says the business went from a team of four to two and had a month in the red, and Ottley builds the missing systems around lead handling and the founder's calendar. The video is 34 minutes and lists his tech stack in the description.
items.author: Liam Ottley
items.enterprise_translation: A one-week rebuild shows how fast a small team can map its work and hand the repeatable parts to agents. Pick one team where everything runs through a single person and sketch which of their weekly jobs an agent could own.

items.title: 2026 AI Horror Film Competition Winners!
items.summary: Curious Refuge crowns the winners of its fourth annual AI Horror Film competition in a 54-minute premiere with celebrity judges, including Promise Studios co-founder Dave Clark. The team says the quality of the films is mind-blowing, and it held an in-person premiere for finalists in Los Angeles that week.
items.author: Curious Refuge
items.enterprise_translation: A themed competition turned filmmakers into a community and a pipeline of finished work. Run a two-week internal build-off on one theme, such as 'fix a customer annoyance', with a premiere night to show the entries.

emerging_signals.pattern: Personal agents are a crowded product category, and creators now publish setup guides within days of each update.
emerging_signals.evidence: Alex Finn on Grok Bot dashboards (Oct 28), Wes Roth's Grok Bot workforce guide (Oct 30), and Riley Brown on texting your ChatGPT Dot from iMessage (Oct 31).

emerging_signals.pattern: Local and open-weight AI is getting more capable and more hardware-friendly.
emerging_signals.evidence: Alex Finn clusters two DGX Sparks for DeepSeek 4.1 Flash, Sam Witteveen tests HP's 748 GB ZGX Fury at a reported 3,000 tokens per second, and Berman calls DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 the best open-source model.

emerging_signals.pattern: Frontier labs are showing AI producing research results, not just summarizing them.
emerging_signals.evidence: Two Minute Papers and TheAIGRID on OpenAI's three discoveries, and Matt Wolfe's weekly roundup, all in the same week.

emerging_signals.pattern: Cheaper computer-use models are arriving next to the premium ones.
emerging_signals.evidence: GPT-6.1 Terra at $1 and $5 per million tokens in Nick Saraev's head-to-head, and Gemini 4 Carbon's launch two weeks after Argon.

emerging_signals.pattern: Claude is moving into creative tools.
emerging_signals.evidence: Skill Leap AI's Blender and Unreal 3D builds, plus Riley Brown's video editing and slide design with Claude, and Curious Refuge's AI relighting tutorial in film.
